# G01 — Error recovery and bounded next actions

## Goal

Every `AppErrorCode` has one stable recovery policy containing:

- `retryable`;
- `scope`, either `self-retry` or `user-action-required`;
- an optional `action` describing the next user- or host-permitted step.

`AppError` exposes `retryable` and `nextAction` while retaining the existing unified
`HostResponse`/`AppError` envelope.

## Recovery contract

The exhaustive source of truth is `APP_ERROR_RECOVERY` in
`src/lib/error-model.ts`. The table is checked with
`Record<AppErrorCode, AppErrorRecovery>`, so adding a code without recovery data
is a compile-time error.

Only transient failures that can safely repeat the same operation are retryable:
`TIMEOUT`, `RATE_LIMIT`, `NETWORK`, `GATEWAY`, and `OVERLOADED`. Their scope is
`self-retry` and their action is exactly:

```ts
{ kind: 'retry' }
```

Every other known class has scope `user-action-required` and a non-retry action.
`UNKNOWN` is not retryable, has no `nextAction`, and is marked
`exposeRawError: true`; it must be surfaced to the user rather than described as
automatically repairable.

## Action vocabulary

`nextAction.kind` is limited to:

- `retry`
- `reauthenticate`
- `reconfigure`
- `open-settings`
- `contact-support`

An action may contain only `kind` and the optional bounded `target`. Targets are
closed enum values such as `authentication`, `configuration`, `model`, and
`billing`. Actions never contain `command`, `script`, `shell`, `exec`, `argv`, or
other executable content.

## Acceptance checks

1. Every code in `APP_ERROR_CODES` has exactly one recovery entry.
2. Retryable entries use `self-retry` and exactly `{ kind: 'retry' }`.
3. Non-retryable known entries use `user-action-required` and never use the
   retry verb.
4. `UNKNOWN` has no action and exposes the original error to the user.
5. Normalization continues to return `AppError`; no second error envelope or
   error class is introduced.
6. Existing error-governance checks, web type checking, scoped lint, harness
   validation/dry-run, and communication replay/compare remain green.

# G01 closure: error recovery and next actions

## Result

`src/lib/error-model.ts` now provides a single, exhaustive recovery policy for all
application error classes. The policy is attached to every `AppError`, exposing
`retryable` and a bounded `nextAction` without changing the existing unified
`HostResponse`/`AppError` envelope.

## Policy

| Code | Retryable | Scope | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AUTH_INVALID` | no | user-action-required | reauthenticate authentication |
| `AUTH_PERMANENT` | no | user-action-required | reauthenticate authentication |
| `TIMEOUT` | yes | self-retry | retry |
| `RATE_LIMIT` | yes | self-retry | retry |
| `PERMISSION` | no | user-action-required | contact-support permissions |
| `CHANNEL_UNAVAILABLE` | no | user-action-required | open-settings channels |
| `CONVERSATION_STATE` | no | user-action-required | reconfigure conversation |
| `NETWORK` | yes | self-retry | retry |
| `CONFIG` | no | user-action-required | reconfigure configuration |
| `GATEWAY` | yes | self-retry | retry |
| `BILLING` | no | user-action-required | open-settings billing |
| `OVERLOADED` | yes | self-retry | retry |
| `MODEL_NOT_FOUND` | no | user-action-required | reconfigure model |
| `UNKNOWN` | no | user-action-required | none; expose raw error |

Only transient, repeatable failures are marked retryable. Their action is
precisely `{ kind: 'retry' }`. All other known failures require an explicit user
action and cannot use the retry verb.

## Safety boundary

The action vocabulary is closed:

`retry`, `reauthenticate`, `reconfigure`, `open-settings`, and `contact-support`.

Only `kind` and a bounded enum-valued `target` are permitted. The model has no
field for commands, scripts, shell text, executables, or argument vectors. This
keeps recovery declarative and prevents an error response from becoming an
instruction channel.

`UNKNOWN` deliberately has no `nextAction`. Its policy sets `exposeRawError` so
callers can show the original failure instead of manufacturing a repair that is
not known to work.

## Compatibility

The implementation extends the existing `AppError`; it does not introduce a
second error type or envelope. Existing cause, details, request ID, structured
signal classification, and normalization behavior are preserved.
